status.title: Status
status.skipped_value: {n} entries could not be decrypted (see the task log for their IDs)
status.check_text: Logged in as {user}: {resources} entries in {folders} folders are visible.
status.check_pinned_now: The server key was pinned now; from now on a different server is refused.

settings.title: Settings
settings.saved: The settings are stored. Check the connection on the status page.
settings.keep: Stored. Leave empty to keep it.
settings.account_help: Use a dedicated Passbolt account that only has read access to the shared folders (see the guide). The export contains exactly what this account can decrypt.
settings.private_key_help: The file "passbolt-recovery-kit.asc" that Passbolt offered when the account was set up. It is stored with the module secrets and never shown again.
settings.private_key_loaded: {name} loaded, will be stored on save
settings.totp_secret_help: Only if the account uses two-factor authentication: the base32 secret shown below the QR code when TOTP is set up in Passbolt. Security keys (WebAuthn) are not supported.
settings.totp_secret_set: Stored. Leave empty to keep it.
settings.ca_pem_help: Only for a private certificate authority: paste its CA certificate in PEM format. It is trusted for Passbolt and for the upload target, in addition to the public ones.
settings.kdbx_help: The export is a KeePass database (KDBX 4, Argon2) that KeePassXC, Strongbox, KeePassDX and others open without a server.
settings.kdbx_password_help: At least 12 characters; a passphrase of several words is easier to keep on paper.
settings.keyfile_help: The key file is generated in this browser and downloaded once. The module keeps a copy to encrypt the next exports, but never uploads it and never shows it again. Without it the file cannot be opened.
settings.keyfile_generated: New key file downloaded, will be stored on save
settings.keyfile_unsaved: The new key file only takes effect after saving. Older exports on the target still need the previous key file.
settings.offline: Write the KeePass password down, keep the key file and the login of the upload target outside Passbolt as well (paper, safe, USB stick), next to the Passbolt recovery kit. If they are only in Passbolt, the emergency copy cannot be opened when it is needed.
settings.target_path_help_folder: Folder on the service; it is created if needed.
settings.oauth_help: Run this on your own computer with rclone installed (rclone.org/downloads), log in in the browser window that opens and allow access:
settings.oauth_help_2: Then paste the whole token printed between the arrows (it starts with a curly bracket) here.
settings.retention_help: After each upload the oldest exports beyond this number are deleted. Only files written by this module are touched.
settings.time_help: HH:MM in the time zone of the node; a run missed while the node was off is caught up.
settings.notify_email_help: Sent through the SMTP smarthost of the cluster after every run. Empty = no mail.
settings.notify_from_help: Empty = the smarthost user, or no-reply at the node name.
settings.error_passbolt_url_invalid: Enter an https:// address without user name, query or fragment
settings.error_ca_pem_invalid: Not a certificate in PEM format
settings.error_private_key_invalid: Not an OpenPGP private key (ASCII armored)
settings.error_keyfile_invalid: Not a valid KeePass key file
settings.error_target_path_invalid: Letters, digits, space and . _ - / only, no ..
settings.error_target_token_required: Paste the token of rclone authorize
settings.error_target_token_invalid: Not a token of rclone authorize
settings.error_onedrive_lookup_failed: The OneDrive of this token could not be found
settings.error_account_incomplete: Store the Passbolt address, key and passphrase first

guide.title: Emergency guide
guide.why_title: Why this module: the circular dependency
guide.why_intro: Many installations keep every password in Passbolt, including the ones needed to bring Passbolt back:
guide.why_1: Passbolt runs on NethServer 8. If the node, its disk or the whole cluster is lost, Passbolt is gone with it.
guide.why_2: To restore NethServer 8 you need the login of the backup destination, the encryption password of the backup repository and an administrator account. They are in Passbolt.
guide.why_3: Even with a restored Passbolt you still need your Passbolt recovery kit (private key) and its passphrase to read anything.
guide.why_4: Result: without NethServer 8 no Passbolt, without Passbolt no way to restore NethServer 8. The module backup of Passbolt does not help, because it can only be used on a running NethServer 8.
guide.why_break: This module breaks the circle: a current, encrypted copy of the passwords lies outside the server, and it opens on any computer or phone with a free KeePass app, without a server and without Passbolt. All you need is the offline emergency kit below.
guide.kit_help: Keep these items outside Passbolt and outside this server, on paper or a USB stick in a safe place:
guide.kit_1: Login of the upload target (for example the Dropbox account), including its two-factor recovery codes.
guide.kit_2: The KeePass password of the export.
guide.kit_3: The key file, if enabled (USB stick, second copy at another place).
guide.kit_4: The Passbolt recovery kit and passphrase of your own account, for the way back to a running Passbolt.
guide.kit_5: Encryption password of the NethServer 8 backup repository and an administrator login of the cluster.
guide.kit_warning: If any of these items exists only in Passbolt, the emergency copy is useless in exactly the case it is made for.
guide.open_title: In an emergency: open the copy
guide.open_1: Log in to the upload target from any computer or phone and download the newest file passbolt-export-YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS.kdbx.
guide.open_2: Install a KeePass app (see below). No account and no server are needed.
guide.open_3: Open the file, enter the KeePass password and, if enabled, select the key file.
guide.open_4: The folders of Passbolt appear as groups. Copy the passwords you need; TOTP codes of entries with two-factor data are shown by the app.
guide.open_5: Work from a copy and do not edit the exported file: the next export replaces it anyway.
guide.checksum_help: The report mail and the status page show the SHA-256 checksum of each export. Compare it with the downloaded file:
guide.app_keepassxc: Windows, macOS, Linux; free and open source (keepassxc.org).
guide.app_keepassdx: Android; free and open source (F-Droid, Google Play).
guide.app_keeweb: In the browser or as desktop app, if nothing can be installed.
guide.account_title: Setting up the export account in Passbolt
guide.account_help: A dedicated account with read access is safer than your own account: it cannot change or delete anything and can be disabled without touching your key.
guide.account_1: As Passbolt administrator, create a user, for example notfall-export, with the role User.
guide.account_2: Open the invitation, finish the setup in a browser with the Passbolt extension and download the recovery kit (passbolt-recovery-kit.asc). Choose a long passphrase.
guide.account_3: If two-factor authentication is required in your Passbolt, enable TOTP for this account and copy the base32 secret shown below the QR code. Security keys are not supported by the export.
guide.account_4: Share your top-level folders with this account with the permission "can read". Items that are later created in or moved into a shared folder through the Passbolt web interface are shared with it as well.
guide.account_5: Personal items that are not in a shared folder are not exported. Move them into a folder (for example "Private") shared read-only with the export account.
guide.account_6: Enter address, recovery kit, passphrase and TOTP secret in the settings, save, then press "Check connection" on the status page. The number of entries must match your expectation.
guide.account_risk: The module stores the private key, passphrase and TOTP secret of this account in its secrets (file readable only by the module, not included in the NS8 backup: after restoring this module from a backup, enter them again). Whoever controls this server can read everything the account can read. That is the price of an automatic export; keep the account read-only.
guide.target_help: Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive and pCloud are connected with a token that rclone creates on your own computer after you log in to the service in your browser:
guide.target_1: Install rclone from rclone.org/downloads (a single program, no setup needed).
guide.target_2: Run the matching command, log in, allow access and copy the token printed in the terminal into the settings.
guide.target_3: The module refreshes the token by itself. If the service revokes it (password change, removed app), create a new one the same way.
guide.test_1: After the setup and then every few months: download the newest file and open it with the offline kit only, on a device that has no access to Passbolt.
guide.test_2: Compare the number of entries with the status page.
guide.test_3: Each export is opened and counted again by the module before upload ("Opened again and checked").
guide.test_4: A failed run is reported by mail; check the status page if a mail is missing.
guide.limits_1: Only what the export account can decrypt is exported.
guide.limits_2: Exported: name, user name, URL, password, description, TOTP data and custom fields. Not exported: comments, tags, sharing permissions and password expiry.
guide.limits_3: The copy is as strong as the KeePass password and the key file. Anyone with both and access to the upload target can read all exported passwords.
guide.limits_4: The export is one-way: it is a reading copy, not a way back into Passbolt. For restoring Passbolt itself use the NethServer 8 backup.
guide.limits_5: Two-factor authentication of the export account works only with TOTP.

sheet.title: Emergency sheet
sheet.intro: Print all secrets of this export on one A4 page, for a sealed envelope in the safe. The page contains:
sheet.content_1: the KeePass password and the key file to type in again
sheet.content_2: storage place, name and SHA-256 of the newest export
sheet.content_3: address, account, passphrase and TOTP secret of the Passbolt export account
sheet.content_4: empty fields for the login of the upload target (user, password, TOTP, recovery codes, token)
sheet.content_5: empty fields for the recovery key of the NethServer 8 backup
sheet.content_6: the steps to open the copy in an emergency
sheet.danger_title: This page opens all exported passwords
sheet.danger: Print it only on a printer you trust, put it in a sealed envelope right away and keep it in a safe. Print it again after changing the KeePass password or the key file.
sheet.pdf: "Print" sends the sheet straight to the printer; no file is created. If you choose "Save as PDF" in the print dialog, that file is NOT encrypted. "Download as encrypted PDF" gives a file protected with AES-256 that opens only with your cluster password.
sheet.admin_password_help: Needed again for every print or download. After 5 wrong attempts the page is locked for 15 minutes.
sheet.done_print: The print dialog was opened. Nothing of the sheet is kept in this page.
sheet.done_key: The recovery kit of the export account was downloaded. It is protected by its passphrase; keep it with the sheet.
sheet.error_sheet_locked: Too many wrong passwords: try again in 15 minutes
sheet.p_step_1: Log in to the upload target and download the newest .kdbx file.
sheet.p_step_2: Install KeePassXC (Windows, macOS, Linux), Strongbox (iOS) or KeePassDX (Android).
sheet.p_step_3: Re-create the key file as described above, open the .kdbx with the KeePass password and the key file.
sheet.p_step_4: Use the NS8 backup key and the passwords in the file to restore NethServer 8 and Passbolt.
sheet.p_footer: After use: print a new sheet, change the passwords that were exposed.
sheet.p_keyfile_how_short: Key file: type the text below into a plain text file "passbolt-export.keyx" (typing errors are caught by the Hash).
sheet.p_keyfile_hex_short: Or: a file with only the 64 characters of the 8 groups, no spaces, no line break at the end. ␣ in a password = space.
sheet.p_private_key_short: file passbolt-recovery-kit-…asc on a USB stick in this envelope
sheet.done_pdf: The PDF was downloaded. It opens only with your cluster password (AES-256). Print it, then delete it, also from the downloads folder and the recycle bin.
